turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Alright Denise, step on the scale for me. 186 pounds. Have a seat and I'll grab the rest of the numbers.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): 186? I was around 170 in the spring. That can't be right, can it?
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Scale's right. Blood pressure is 128 over 84, pulse 58, temperature 36.7 Celsius, oxygen 99 percent. You're looking pretty wound up.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I am wound up. I've been so tired, and I'm cold all the time, socks and a sweater and it's June. Is 58 too low, am I going to pass out?
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She will not take that sweater off. I'm Ray, her husband. I booked this because she keeps saying it's nothing.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Dr. Shah is finishing a note. Want some water? Fair warning, the cooler has been spitting lukewarm stuff all week.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Water's fine. Um, my mood's been in the basement, but I think that's the job. I'm 51, I manage a call center, the hours are stupid, things just wear out.
[SEG0008] person_1 (NURSE): Don't apologize for any of it. She'll be right in.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Denise, I'm Dr. Shah. Tired and cold, that's the headline. How long has the tiredness been going on?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): About three months, since this project at work blew up.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three months? No. She's been dragging since last summer. That's eight or nine months, easy.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, maybe it wasn't just three. I, um, lose track. Work makes it worse, so I pin it on work.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): He says last summer, you say three months, so that's not nailed down. Cold for whatever that stretch is?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. The whole time. Hands and feet mostly. Could it be my circulation? Do I need a scan?
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not ordering a scan. I'll check a TSH and see you in three months. This sounds like the hours.

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Three months? I can barely finish a shift. And I've gained all this weight, like fifteen or sixteen pounds, and I'm not even eating more. Well, crackers at my desk, do those count?
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Crackers aren't a buffet, but her bowels are a mess, that's what she won't lead with.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Constipation?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Every few days, and it's hard. I bought MiraLAX and took one capful, one time, and then I chickened out.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the stool?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None. I googled cancer at two in the morning and now I'm scared. I was gonna say I can't sleep, but that's not true, I sleep and I just wake up tired.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Short of breath?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I can walk fine. I'm just wiped after.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tell her about the crying at night. She's not herself.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): My mood is low. I cry at commercials. I'm not unsafe, I would tell you if I was. It's the ten-hour days.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any thoughts of hurting yourself?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Absolutely not. Please don't just call this depression and wave me out. My mom had a thyroid problem, she was on that thyroid pill for years, and I never took hers.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Have you had your own thyroid blood test?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. They said borderline. Two years ago, or maybe longer, I can't remember the year. I'm sure they said borderline.
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The letter said normal, Denise. You called it borderline anyway. I think that paper is still in the drawer at home.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): It said normal? Oh, shoot. Maybe I have that wrong. What if I've been blowing off something real this whole time?

[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm not hanging a diagnosis on a letter neither of you brought. Tired, cold, weight up, constipated, low mood, mother with thyroid disease — could be an underactive thyroid, could be anemia, could still be the job. I will not conclude which one today.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): So you do think it's my thyroid? Do I start the medicine my mom was on, the levo-something? What if waiting makes it worse?
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): No levothyroxine today. And scratch the TSH-only visit in three months. I said that before the weight, the bowels, and your mom.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Scratch it how? Is three months dangerous? What if I faint at my desk?
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Blood this week: TSH, a free T4, and a CBC. I'll see you back in two weeks with the results. Not three months.
[SEG0041] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She also takes the purple pill every morning, for her heartburn.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Nexium, the purple one, forty milligrams. I skip a lot of mornings when I'm running late. Does that ruin the blood test? Should I even take it today?
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): It will not ruin the thyroid test. Keep taking it when you remember. I'm not changing that pill. What else is in the cabinet?

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Zoloft. They started it, I think at fifty milligrams, or maybe it was twenty-five, I never wrote it down. I stopped it in March after about two weeks. It made me feel buzzy.
[SEG0045] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And Colace. Some other doctor wrote it. She never picked it up.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Right, I never took Colace. Should I have? Is MiraLAX safer, and should I restart the Zoloft? My sister swears by hers.
[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do not restart the Zoloft on your own. Leave that one capful of MiraLAX as a one-time thing. I am not prescribing Colace today.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. I don't have any allergies, I'm allergic to nothing. My shins itch. Is that the thyroid, and are you gonna biopsy me?
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): No drug allergies. Thyroid feels normal size, no nodules, so no biopsy. Pulse is regular. Skin on the shins is dry, and that's the whole exam.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Is a pulse of 58 too slow? What if the CBC is awful? Can they draw it today, and will the needle hurt?
[SEG0051] person_1 (NURSE): Lab's open till four. I can walk you down when you're done.
[SEG0052] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll go with her. The parking garage was a nightmare, by the way. We come back in two weeks either way, right?
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): A pulse of 58 can be normal, and the CBC is to look for anemia. Two weeks with me. If they can't draw you today, still get it this week, and don't slide past Friday.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
